newsitem.title: CANADA: Rain slows Alberta harvest, frost damage occurs.
newsitem.headline: Rain slows Alberta harvest, frost damage occurs.

text.p: Rain and damp conditions slowed much of Alberta's harvesting this week, according to the Alberta Wheat Pool's weekly report.
Frost damaged some late-maturing crops and snow was reported with eastern areas reporting crops flattened by snow.
Grade estimates moved down for many crops.

As of Thursday 47 percent of provincial harvest was completed versus the 10-year average of 69 percent. Harvest was nearly done in the southern regions, while in central and northern areas "up to four weeks of warm dry weather" were needed to complete the harvest.

The harvest pace versus year ago was: hard red spring wheat 42 vs 73; Canada prairie spring wheat 28 vs 67, soft white spring wheat 89 vs 87, winter wheat 100 vs 98, durum wheat 80 vs 66, oats 28 vs 71, barley 54 vs 73, flax 26 vs 22, fall rye 83 vs 100, and canola 48 vs 74.

Grade estimates versus the 10-year averages include: No.1 Canadian western red spring (CWRS) 35 vs 50; No.2 CWRS 21 vs 24; No. 3 CWRS 28 vs 30; and feed wheat 16 vs 16. Malting barley 19 vs 13; No.1 Canadian Western (CW) barley 70 vs 71; No.2 CW 10 vs 16. No. 1 Canada canola 81 vs 72; No. 2 Canada canola 14 vs 17; No. 3 Canada three vs 7 and sample one vs four.
